newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel oil boosted by paper, US/Asian strength.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel oil boosted by paper, US/Asian strength.

text.p: European fuel oil prices were boosted on Friday by higher swaps, which had risen on the back of soaring crude and the strength of Asian and U.S. markets, traders said.

Dutch dealers returned from their Ascension day break to find Rotterdam barges $4 stronger, trading at $86 and $86.50 fob on short covering, after swaps leapt up on Thursday in response to Singapore's strength.
Some 20,000 tonnes traded in the morning, a high level given the absence of the majors, many of whom had taken the Friday off.
"It's more bullish than we've been for a while," said one trader. Another added that he did not expect the rise to continue, despite IPE Brent's continued push towards $19.
"I think $87 is the top. When the majors come into the office on Monday we'll probably see it head back down," he said.

Low sulphur cargoes are still tight in the prompt period, but demand is slight and prices were slow to respond to the rise in cargo swaps. One dealer pegged physical one percent notionally up $1 at $87/$88 fob.
The bullish trend was scaring high sulphur cargo buyers away from the market and material was believed flowing out of the region.
